# AI Resume Analyzer

An AI-powered web application that compares your resume against a job description.
Create an account, upload a PDF resume, paste in the job description, and get a
**match score**, a **skill-gap analysis** (matched vs. missing skills), and
**personalized AI feedback** generated by a large language model. Every analysis is
saved to your account so you can review, track, or delete it later.

Built with **Flask**, backed by **PostgreSQL** (via Flask-SQLAlchemy), and powered by
the **Groq** API.

## Features

- **User Accounts** – Sign up and log in with email and password; passwords are hashed with Werkzeug and protected pages require an active session.
- **Resume Match Score** – See how closely your resume matches the job requirements with a percentage score and a compatibility ring.
- **Skill Gap Analysis** – Automatically detects the skills present in your resume and highlights the ones missing for the role.
- **Multi-Step Analyze Wizard** – A guided flow (upload resume → add job description → review & analyze) with drag-and-drop upload, a live character counter, and one-click sample job descriptions.
- **Resume Preview** – Open your uploaded PDF right from the results page.
- **AI Resume Feedback** – Get a structured, plain-text analysis with Strengths, Weaknesses, Missing Skills (with reasoning), and Suggestions for Improvement, rendered as clean feedback cards.
- **Analysis History** – Every analysis is stored in PostgreSQL against your account; browse past scores and delete records you no longer need.
- **Clean Dashboard UI** – A responsive workspace with an animated "analyzing…" state while the analysis runs.

---

## How It Works

```
Sign up / Log in                     (app.py  -> User, hashed password)
        │
        ▼
Upload PDF resume + Job description  (templates/analyzer.html + wizard.js)
        │
        ▼
Extract text from the PDF            (src/resume_parser.py  -> PyPDF2)
        │
        ▼
Extract skills from the resume       (src/resume_parser.py  -> regex section match)
        │
        ▼
Extract required skills from the JD  (src/job_matcher.py    -> keyword list)
        │
        ▼
Calculate match score                (src/scoring.py        -> matched / missing)
        │
        ▼
Save the result to history           (models.py -> AnalysisHistory)
        │
        ▼
AI analysis (Strengths, Weaknesses,  (src/ai_analyzer.py    -> Groq LLM)
Missing Skills, Suggestions)
        │
        ▼
Render results on the dashboard      (templates/index.html)
```

| Database      | PostgreSQL via Flask-SQLAlchemy         |

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- Python 3.11+ (the pinned `pandas==3.0.5` requires Python ≥ 3.11; `Flask==3.1.2` requires ≥ 3.9)
- A [Groq](https://console.groq.com/keys) API key (free tier available)
- A **PostgreSQL** database URL (e.g. a free [Render](https://render.com) or [Neon](https://neon.tech) instance)

### 1. Clone the repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/RitamNaskar11/Resume_analyzer.git
cd Resume_analyzer
```

### 2. Create and activate a virtual environment

**Windows (PowerShell):**

```powershell
python -m venv venv
.\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
```

**macOS / Linux:**

```bash
python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
```

### 3. Install dependencies

Install everything from `requirements.txt`:

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

The file pins the following packages:

| Package           | Version | Purpose                              |
| ----------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Flask             | 3.1.2   | Web framework and routing            |
| Flask-SQLAlchemy  | (any)   | ORM for the PostgreSQL database      |
| psycopg2-binary   | (any)   | PostgreSQL database driver           |
| PyPDF2            | 3.0.1   | PDF text extraction                  |
| groq              | 1.7.0   | Groq API client for the LLM          |
| python-dotenv     | 1.2.3   | Loads `.env` variables               |
| gunicorn          | 26.2.0  | Production WSGI server               |
| pandas            | 3.0.5   | Data utilities                       |
| matplotlib        | 3.11.1  | Plotting library                     |

### 4. Configure environment variables

Create a `.env` file in the project root:

```env
GROQ_API_KEY=your_groq_api_key_here
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@host:5432/dbname
SECRET_KEY=some-long-random-string
```

- `GROQ_API_KEY` – read via `os.getenv("GROQ_API_KEY")`; required for the AI feedback step.
- `DATABASE_URL` – read via `os.environ.get("DATABASE_URL")`; a `postgres://` prefix is automatically rewritten to `postgresql://` (handy for Render-style URLs).
- `SECRET_KEY` – used to sign the session cookie; falls back to `dev-secret-key` when unset, so set a real value in production.

### 5. Run the application

```bash
python app.py
```

On startup the app creates any missing tables (`db.create_all()`) and prints
`PostgreSQL database connected successfully!`. Then open your browser at:

```
http://127.0.0.1:5000
```

### 6. Deploy (optional)

`requirements.txt` includes **Gunicorn**, so the app can also run behind a WSGI
server on a host such as Render:

```bash
gunicorn app:app
```

Set `GROQ_API_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, and `SECRET_KEY` as environment variables in your
hosting provider's dashboard.

## Usage

1. **Sign up** for an account, then **log in**.
2. From the dashboard, click **Start Analyzing** (or **Analyze resume** in the sidebar).
3. **Step 1** — upload your resume as a **PDF** (drag-and-drop or browse; max 5 MB).
4. **Step 2** — paste the **job description**, or pick a one-click sample (Frontend, Backend, Data Scientist, ML Engineer).
5. **Step 3** — review your inputs and click **Analyze Resume**.
6. Review the results:
   - **Match Score** (%) with a compatibility ring and a matched / missing / required summary.
   - **Matched Skills**, **Missing Skills**, and **Skills in your resume**.
   - **Resume Preview** — open your uploaded PDF.
   - **AI Resume Analysis** — Strengths, Weaknesses, Missing Skills, and Suggestions for Improvement.
7. Visit **Analysis history** to revisit or **delete** previous analyses.

> Uploads are validated (PDF only, 5 MB max) in the browser and again on submit.

## API Routes

| Method | Route                          | Description                                                        |
| ------ | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| GET    | `/`                            | Redirects to `/dashboard` when logged in, otherwise to `/login`    |
| GET    | `/signup`                      | Renders the sign-up page                                           |
| POST   | `/signup`                      | Creates a new user (hashes the password, rejects duplicate emails) |
| GET    | `/login`                       | Renders the login page                                             |
| POST   | `/login`                       | Authenticates a user and starts a session                          |
| GET    | `/logout`                      | Clears the session and redirects to login                          |
| GET    | `/dashboard`                   | Welcome / start screen (login required)                            |
| GET    | `/analyzer`                    | Multi-step analyze wizard (login required)                         |
| POST   | `/analyze`                     | Accepts the resume + job description, runs the analysis, saves history |
| GET    | `/results`                     | Shows the latest analysis from the session (login required)        |
| GET    | `/history`                     | Lists the current user's previous analyses (login required)        |
| POST   | `/delete_analysis/<record_id>` | Deletes one of the current user's history records (login required) |
| GET    | `/uploads/<filename>`          | Serves an uploaded resume file (used for the preview)              |

### Database Models (`models.py`)

- **`User`** — `id`, `name`, `email` (unique), `password` (Werkzeug hash), `created_at`.
- **`AnalysisHistory`** — `id`, `user_id` (FK → `users.id`), `filename`, `score`, `matched_skills` (JSON), `missing_skills` (JSON), `created_at`.

Tables are created automatically on the first run via `db.create_all()`.

---

## Notes & Limitations

- Resumes must be in **PDF** format and contain an extractable text layer (scanned/image-only PDFs will not work without OCR).
- Resume skill extraction relies on a dedicated **"Skills"** section in the resume; resumes without such a heading may return few or no skills.
- Job skill extraction matches against a **predefined keyword list** in `src/job_matcher.py` — currently: Python, AWS, SQL, C++, Django, Go, JavaScript, Machine Learning, Bootstrap, and GitHub. Extend this list to support more technologies.
- Results are held in the **session**, so once the session ends `/results` redirects back to the analyzer.
- Uploaded resumes are stored in the shared `uploads/` folder by filename, so re-uploading a file with the same name overwrites the previous one.
- `templates/landing.html` (with `static/landing.css`) is a marketing page that exists but is **not wired to any route** yet — `/` redirects straight to login.
- The AI analysis requires a valid `GROQ_API_KEY`; the rest of the pipeline works without it.
- `requirements.txt` is saved as **UTF-16 (with BOM)**, so some editors may display it oddly — `pip install -r requirements.txt` still works.
